correctness.rationale: Every finite word has a unique greedy embedding of each distinct double-deletion descendant. Explicit enumeration of the four possibilities for two omitted positions gives B=binom(K,2)+n-1-J. Uniform random letters make adjacent-inequality indicators iid Bernoulli(p) and distance-two equality indicators marginally jointly independent Bernoulli(1/q), with the unique covariance interaction occurring for two adjacent inequalities. The variance identity follows by a complete binomial covariance calculation. For q~n/theta, mixed factorial moments of adjacent and lag-two equality counts converge to theta^(a+b); every graph component with at least two edges has at least three vertices and vanishes as O(n/q^2), yielding independent Poisson limits. The exact deficit identity then supplies both scales; full-volume enumeration supplies e^(-2theta). Exhaustive finite checks across 39,669 center words match local counts and exact rational moments. No finite experiment is used as proof of an infinite limit.

originality.rationale: The 2026 q-ary deletion-reconstruction source addresses intersections of two deletion balls, not variance of a randomly chosen single-center two-deletion sphere. A fully inspected public 2026 binary-variance manuscript supplies the q=2 specialization but explicitly excludes nonbinary alphabets. The 2018 full-text study of random subsequences counts total expected subsequences, not exactly-two-deletion variances or a two-scale joint Poisson limit. The independent-Poisson correction has a different quantified domain and cannot be obtained by merely inserting q into the established binary Walsh identity. Searches do not prove global novelty, but no stronger implication covering the asserted q>=3 variance plus growing-q limit was identified.
residual_risks: An unindexed nonbinary moment formula or growing-alphabet Poisson limit may exist despite the searches.
The deterministic local identity might follow from older general subsequence enumeration, and is used as a lemma rather than promoted as independent originality.
The Swart--Ferreira source is credited through a full-text secondary mathematical quotation, rather than direct full-text inspection.

value.rationale: The two-deletion sphere volume governs how many distinct readouts a transmitted codeword can produce and is a natural channel-geometric invariant. Beyond the known binary variance, the closed nonbinary variance and, especially, a joint independent-Poisson first/second-scale crossover at q proportional to n reveal how local letter repeats determine typical ambiguity. The exact e^(-2theta) fraction of maximal spheres gives a natural reliability threshold for growing alphabets. This is an infinite-parameter structural distribution theorem, not an arbitrary low-dimensional census.
